findings.desc: Transient polling failures deleted the durable theme handle.
Guided revisions did not persist or resume their async job.
Older reload and pagination responses could overwrite a newer filter generation.
Multiple report statuses could be submitted concurrently from one DOM group.
A ready job handle was removed before its in-memory draft was built.
No durable identity existed before the first POST response arrived.
Older guided revision responses could overwrite a newer revision.
Rapid armed takedown or restore taps could launch concurrent mutations.
A rerender could bypass report-resolution exclusivity tied to old DOM nodes.
A hung theme polling GET had no timeout or abort path.
Revision tokens could collide with a later package generation token.
Building a safe candidate did not invalidate the still-running guided generation.
The poll limit did not enforce its intended absolute wall-clock deadline.
A repaint could recreate the other feed pagination button while its request remained in flight.
Moderation list GETs had no bounded timeout or abort path.
A suspended WebView could resume after the polling deadline and still run a full-timeout GET.
